category_title: Children with communication difficulties and reactive behavioral outbursts
minimal_context: Angus is participating in a group discussion about the story Laura and Paul where students must raise their hands to contribute.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start our group discussion about the story Laura and Paul. Remember to raise your hand if you wish to contribute.

STUDENT: (Raises hand and speaks very quickly) I know what happened! Once that thought is in your head it’s a brilliant thing. It’s a brilliant thought!

TUTOR: Thank you. Sarah just mentioned that she disagrees with your view on the story.

STUDENT: (Looks flustered) But... no! Wait, I lost what I was going to say. She's wrong!

TUTOR: What do you want to say back to her?

STUDENT: (Makes an angry face and shouts out) Shut up! (Kicks the desk) I'm not talking to you!

options.A: Project the story of Laura and Paul from slides on the big screen in the classroom, adding sound effects and motion features.
options.B: Explicitly teach that readers can have the same facts but different interpretations, using the students' views on the story as an example of subjectivity.
options.C: Have the student listen to the story of Laura and Paul for a second time before continuing the group discussion.
options.D: Take responsibility as the facilitator to ensure a balanced dialogue occurs where as many perspectives as possible are explored.
